title: Nehemiah 12:12–26
context: This list names the heads of priestly families in the days of the high priest Joiakim, following the order of 12:1–7 with some differences in name and form, and then notes records of Levites and priests kept down to the reign of Darius the Persian. The chiefs of the Levites, the singers who gave thanks according to David’s commandment, and the gatekeepers are named, and the section closes by dating them to the days of Joiakim, Nehemiah the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe. Both traditions read the lists as shared ground on ordered worship, and the differences from 12:1–7 and Nehemiah 10 are noted without harmonizing.

verses.text: In the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers’ households: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
verses.arminianNotes:
“In the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers” households: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah.’ Arminian readers note that the list moves forward a generation, naming a head for each house.

The order follows 12:1–7.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see the priestly houses carried on into the next generation.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: faithful service is passed on, and each house has a leader in its time.

verses.text: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan.” Arminian readers note that the house of Ezra here is the priestly family named in 12:1.

The list continues the pattern of house and head.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see the same orderly record of priestly families.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the names show worship continuing through ordinary families, not only through famous leaders.

verses.text: of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph.” Arminian readers note that 12:2–3 has Malluch and Shecaniah in the corresponding places.

The differences in form are left unresolved.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note the variation between the two lists.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the records were kept carefully, even where names appear in different forms.

verses.text: of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai.” Arminian readers note that 12:3 has Rehum and Meremoth at about this point.

Nehemiah 10:5 lists both Harim and Meremoth among the priests who sealed the covenant.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers also note the differences between the lists and do not harmonize them.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the priestly families named here continued to serve the restored temple.

verses.text: of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam.” Arminian readers note that this Zechariah of the house of Iddo is often identified with the prophet (Zech 1:1).

The identification is a common reading, not certain.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see a link between priesthood and prophecy in the restored community, as a reading.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the prophets Haggai and Zechariah encouraged the rebuilding (Ezra 5:1).

verses.text: of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai.” Arminian readers note that no head is named for Miniamin, so a name appears to be missing.

The gap is noted without reconstruction.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note the apparent gap in the list.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the list is preserved as it stands, and its gaps do not affect its witness to ordered worship.

verses.text: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan.” Arminian readers note the continuing list of priestly houses and their heads.

Both houses appear in 12:5–6.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see continuity between the two generations of priests.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the houses that went up with Zerubbabel continued to serve in Joiakim’s time.

verses.text: of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi.” Arminian readers note that the priestly divisions of Joiarib and Jedaiah are among the oldest named (cf. 1 Chr 24:7).

The list preserves those ancient houses.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see continuity with the order established in David’s time.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the restored community saw its worship as continuous with the worship of earlier Israel.

verses.text: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber.” Arminian readers note that 12:7 has Sallu where this verse has Sallai.

The difference in form is minor and left unresolved.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the same families continuing.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: each house is named, and each head is remembered, as part of the community’s record.

verses.text: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
verses.arminianNotes:
The list continues, “of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.” Arminian readers note that the list ends with the second Jedaiah of 12:7.

The list for Joiakim’s day closes here.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see the full set of priestly houses accounted for, with the exception of Hattush and the gap in 12:17.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the record serves the ordering of worship.

verses.text: As for the Levites, in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, there were recorded the heads of fathers’ households; also the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.
verses.arminianNotes:
The heads of the Levites and the priests were recorded “in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua... in the reign of Darius the Persian.” Arminian readers note that the records extend later than Nehemiah’s own time.

Which Darius is meant is debated.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note that the dating of this notice is discussed.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the record-keeping continued across several generations of priests.

verses.text: The sons of Levi, heads of fathers’ households, were written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.
verses.arminianNotes:
“The sons of Levi, heads of fathers’ households, were written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.” Arminian readers note the reference to an official record.

This “book of the chronicles” is not necessarily the biblical book of Chronicles.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see careful record-keeping as part of maintaining ordered worship.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the writer draws on records to show continuity, and Johanan is here called the son of Eliashib.

verses.text: The chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers close to them, to praise and give thanks according to the commandment of David the man of God, section next to section.
verses.arminianNotes:
The chiefs of the Levites praise and give thanks “according to the commandment of David the man of God, section next to section.” Arminian readers note the arrangement of singers in groups (cf. 1 Chr 16:4; 25:1).

The phrase may describe singing in alternating groups.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see worship ordered according to the pattern David established.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: praise and thanksgiving are central, and they are offered in an orderly way.

verses.text: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers keeping the watch at the storehouses of the gates.
verses.arminianNotes:
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub “were gatekeepers keeping the watch at the storehouses of the gates.” Arminian readers note that Talmon and Akkub are family names in the return lists (Ezra 2:42; Neh 7:45).

Gatekeeping was part of the temple’s service.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see the guarding of the storehouses as faithful service.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: humble, watchful work protects what is given for God’s house.

verses.text: These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe.
verses.arminianNotes:
“These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe.” Arminian readers note that Ezra and Nehemiah are named together, as in 8:9.

The list is dated by both priestly and civil leaders.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see God’s provision of leaders for both worship and governance.

Both traditions treat this as shared ground: the section closes by placing the lists in the time of the rebuilt community.
